content:
alice: quick RFC thread — proposal for Dedicated->Hosted spillover behaviour and telemetry so we can keep tenant isolation guarantees while still allowing safe spillover. main goals: preserve billing/quotas, surface why fallback happened, avoid accidental data egress for customers with strict controls.

ben: +1 to telemetry. can you paste the proposed routing header + tags?

alice: sure. basic idea: propagate two headers when we hand off a request: X-Tenant-Origin (tenant_id), X-Tenant-Acct-Type (tier: free/standard/enterprise). also attach runtime tags to each span: "tenant_origin", "fallback_reason", "variant_chain". quick policy snippet: 
```json
{
  "route_priority": ["dedicated_pool", "region_local_hosted", "compatible_hosted_variant"],
  "fallback_rules": {
    "evict_on_latency": 0.95,
    "evict_on_util": 0.9,
    "prefer_variant": ["quantized-compatible", "fp16-hosted"]
  },
  "propagate_headers": ["X-Tenant-Origin","X-Tenant-Acct-Type"]
}
```

chris: semantics question: if we add X-Tenant-Origin on hosted, does that make it data egress? legal flagged that any tenant metadata leaving the VPC is sensitive for some customers.

security-bot: flagged by security: PII policy says tenant identifiers may be allowed if pseudonymized and logged. we need a plan for pseudonymization + opt-out.

priya: for EU customers we should avoid sending tenant raw ids — propose sending hashed_tenant_id and a boolean "is_enterprise". also whitelist only for tenants with spillover enabled.

alice: agreed. update: propagate X-Tenant-Hash, X-Tenant-Flags (json-string boolean fields). we should store original->hash mapping only in control plane auditing and never log the raw id in hosted logs.

marco: on fallback ordering: prefer compatible quantized variant on dedicated first, then hosted quantized, then hosted fp16. but if the tenant has "no_hosted_spillover":true, we need to respect that immediately and fail with a 409 and an explicit error body.

dana: UI/Console implications: add a per-tenant toggle under "Routing & Failover" with 3 options: Block, Allow (conservative), Allow (best-effort). default is Allow (conservative). rollout via feature flag. smaller teams should get a per-project notice.

ben: telemetry — we need fields in the per-request trace: tenant_hash, path_chain (e.g., dedicated->hosted->variant), fallback_reason enum (capacity|latency|policy|version-mismatch), and cost_estimate flag so billing can attribute extra tokens. also surface counts on the console: spillover_rate, avg_fallback_latency.

chris: we must be careful with cost attribution: if hosted serves tokens for a dedicated tenant, is it billed against the tenant's reserved pool or their hosted usage? finance prefers it billed to tenant committed capacity first, then fall back to hosted credits. need explicit mapping.

alice: agreed — policy should set fallback_billing: ["dedicated_commit", "hosted_overage"]. and we add an audit event when we switch billing bucket.

priya: telemetry example (span tags): 
```text
trace.span.tags:
  tenant_hash: "sha256:abcd..."
  route: "dedicated_pool"
  fallback_reason: "capacity"
  variant_chain: "dedicated-q8->hosted-q8->hosted-fp16"
  billing_bucket: "dedicated_commit"
```

infra-bot: FYI: i'm going to add a new metric prefix `routing.spillover.<tenant_hash>.count` which will be high-cardinality. recommend we sample for non-enterprise tenants to avoid metric explosion.

marco: sampling is fine. enterprise customers get full visibility. for others we keep 1% sampling. add a console checkbox "detailed spillover metrics" per tenant.

dana: on rollouts UX: when enabling spillover for a tenant, show a modal with three consequences: potential egress, billing fallback, and best-effort latency. include a link to the policy JSON and an "audit-only" trial mode for 24h where we log simulated fallbacks but don't actually hand off.

ben: good idea — audit-only will help customers opt-in safely. Also add a system alert if we start serving >5% tokens from hosted for a dedicated tenant in an hour.

alice: restating action items: 
1) change headers to pseudonymized X-Tenant-Hash + flags (priya)
2) add trace/span tags for fallback_reason, variant_chain, billing_bucket (ben)
3) console toggle + audit-only mode + modal copy (dana)
4) enforce tenant-level guard for "no_hosted_spillover" and return 409 (marco)
5) metric sampling defaults and enterprise opt-in (infra-bot + marco)
6) legal/security review for hashing and retention (security-bot)

security-bot: will take point on review. recommend retention windows: raw mapping 30d in control plane with strict access, hosted logs never contain raw ids, and hashes rotate every 90d.

priya: one more thing — model-compatibility check must live in the routing loop: if a model variant is API-incompatible (different tokenizer or special tokens), we should not fallback to it; instead mark fallback_reason: version-mismatch. we need an early reject before handshake to avoid bad responses.

chris: can we add a lightweight compatibility matrix in the catalog that the router queries with TTL 60s? router should be able to test quickly.

alice: yes. we'll add a compatibility cache and an endpoint /internal/model-compatibility?model_a=...&model_b=... with cached responses. cache invalidation on model rollouts.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature/tenant-spillover-controls -> staging (hashing + telemetry schema) by @alice.

ben: timeline? we'd like staging in 3 days and canary on 10% traffic in a week.

alice: ok. I'll split into three PRs: routing + headers, telemetry tags + metrics, console + feature flag. aiming for staged canary next week.

marco: assign me for the server-side guard and billing mapping.

priya: i'll write the privacy blurb for the modal and the audit-only behavior.

security-bot: noted — i'll run a brief threat model once PRs land.

alice: thanks all. if no objections by EOD I'll open the RFC and start PR 1. :thumbsup:

chris: no objections. :+1:

ben: :thumbsup:

priya: go for it.

marco: LGTM

infra-bot: metric changes recorded: routing.spillover.sample_rate default=0.01 for non-enterprise.

alice: filing RFC now — will paste link in thread when ready.
